Clonotrace

Clonotrace is a package for multimodal analysis of single cell RNA-seq data with lineage information, including lineaged-barcoded cells and immune cells. Clonotrace generates an informative clone embedding to show the clonal dynamics, and extend to pseudotime inference and fate driving gene detection.

Installation

Clonotrace uses packages from both CRAN and Bioconductor. Install it through BiocManager, which resolves Bioconductor dependencies such as rhdf5 and bluster in a compatible release:

if (!requireNamespace("BiocManager", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("BiocManager")
if (!requireNamespace("remotes", quietly = TRUE))
  install.packages("remotes")

BiocManager::install(c("rhdf5", "bluster"))
remotes::install_github("yuntianf/Clonotrace", dependencies = TRUE)

To verify the installation in a clean R session:

library(Clonotrace)
BiocManager::valid()

The Python projection of the optional clone-weighted cell embedding requires the packages in requirements.txt. Install them into an environment you manage, then point reticulate to that environment if it is not selected automatically:

pip install -r requirements.txt

The core Clonotrace workflow does not require Python.

Version 1.2.1 highlights

  • clone_disance() returns a revised clone distance by default: the original Clonotrace distance, globally median-normalized, is blended with clone-centroid distance at a fate-blind, multiresolution RNA-structure-selected weight. Clone-specific local rescaling is optional and disabled by default in version 1.2.1 because it can change neighbour rankings; set local_rescale = TRUE only for a documented sensitivity analysis or to reproduce version 1.2.0. The raw distance remains available in dis_clonotrace or via revised = FALSE.
  • label_spreading_bootstrap() uses the memory-conscious HDF5-backed blocked implementation by default; use backend = "dense" only for legacy reproduction or small inputs.
  • clone_disance(exact = TRUE) now uses the disk-backed exact-OT workflow by default. Its reusable components are build_graph_distance_store() and graph_clone_ot_disk(). The workflow computes the same unregularized graph-Wasserstein distance as the in-memory implementation while replacing the full in-memory cell-distance matrix with a resumable binary store and bounded reads. The tradeoff is quadratic disk space in the stored clone-bearing cells; approximate distance remains the recommended default for routine large datasets. Set exact_backend = "memory" only to reproduce the former dense implementation on a small input.

See NEWS.md, VERSION_REPORT_1.2.0.md, and VERSION_REPORT_1.2.1.md for the complete change and compatibility reports.

Documentation

The documentation and tutorial are available at: https://yuntianf.github.io/Clonotrace/

The tutorial recommends approximate clone-distance calculation for routine analyses and documents both validated checkpoints and the disk-backed exact-OT workflow for reference calculations. A compiled copy is included at vignettes/Clonotrace.html; the GitHub Pages site can be built into docs/ with pkgdown::build_site().

Citation

If you use Clonotrace for published work, please cite our manuscript:

Fu Y, Mathew D, Wang M, et al. Deciphering Cell Fate and Clonal Dynamics via Integrative Single-Cell Lineage Modeling[J]. bioRxiv, 2025: 2025.09. 01.673503.
